title: Wāyid ʿalēk! Saying the opposite
goal: In the university library, your classmate Mājid turns up late to your group project with one slide; tease him with irony, then share out the work
tip: Irony says the opposite with a straight face. To a friend who has done almost nothing: wāyid ʿalēk! 'steady on, don't overdo it!' (lit. it's too much for you). Mock sympathy works the same way: majhūd? yā ḥalīlak! 'effort? you poor thing!'. Use it with friends who can laugh back.
grammar: irony: saying the opposite of what you mean (wāyid ʿalēk)
dialogue: A
هلا! سوري تأخرت، بس ترا خلصت الشريحة حقي
hala! sōri taʼakhkhart, bas tara khallaṣt ish-sharīḥa ḥaggi
Hi! Sorry I'm late, but I've finished my slide, you know.
B
شريحة وحدة في أسبوع؟ وايد عليك!
sharīḥa waḥda fi usbūʿ? wāyid ʿalēk!
One slide in a week? Steady on, don't wear yourself out! (ironic)
A
لا تتطنز علي! سهرت عليها، وهذا مجهود
la titṭannaz ʿalay! sihart ʿalēha, w hādha majhūd
Don't make fun of me! I stayed up late on it; that's real effort.
B
مجهود؟ يا حليلك! فيه ضغط وايد، لازم ترتاح
majhūd? yā ḥalīlak! fīh ẓaghiṭ wāyid, lāzim tirtāḥ
Effort? You poor thing! That's a lot of pressure; you must have a rest. (ironic)
A
خلاص، فهمت! وشو تبيني أسوي في الباقي؟
khalāṣ, fhimt! w shu tabīni asawwi fi l-bāgi?
All right, I get it! So what do you want me to do with the rest?
B
الخاتمة عليك، وتقدم العرض قدام الدكتور. لا تتهرب!
il-khātma ʿalēk, w tgaddim il-ʿarẓ jiddām id-daktōr. la titharrab!
The conclusion's yours, and you give the presentation in front of the lecturer. Don't try to dodge it!
A
بروحي؟ خيبة! يعني انت ما بتقول ولا كلمة؟ تعال حبيبي!
b-rūḥi? khēba! yaʿni inta ma bitgūl wala kilma? taʿāl ḥabībi!
On my own? Come off it! So you won't say a single word? Nice try, mate!
B
أمزح وياك. أنا بقدم النص الأول، والأسئلة في الآخر عليك
amzaḥ wiyyāk. ana bagaddim in-nuṣṣ il-awwal, w il-asʼila fi l-ākhir ʿalēk
I'm joking. I'll present the first half, and the questions at the end are yours.
A
زين. والكرك علي بعدين، عشان ما تقول إني ما سويت شي
zēn. w il-karak ʿalay baʿdēn, ʿashān ma tgūl inni ma sawwēt shay
Fine. And the karak's on me afterwards, so you can't say I did nothing.
B
كرك بعد؟ هذا من طيبك! وايد عليك اليوم
karak baʿad? hādha min ṭībak! wāyid ʿalēk il-yōm
Karak too? That's so kind of you! You're really overdoing it today! (ironic)
items: (ironic) steady on, don't overdo it! (to a man) (friends only)
to a woman: wāyid ʿalēch (وايد عليج); lit. 'it's too much for you', said when someone has done very little
don't make fun of me (to a man)
to a woman: la titṭannazīn ʿalay (لا تتطنزين علي)
the conclusion (of a talk or an essay)
don't try to dodge it, don't wriggle out of it (to a man)
to a woman: la titharrabīn (لا تتهربين)
(sarcastic) nice try, mate! come off it! (to a man) (friends only)
(recognise); to a woman: taʿāli ḥabībti (تعالي حبيبتي); said straight, it's a friendly 'come here, mate'
culture: Wāyid ʿalēk works because everyone knows it means the opposite of its words: said with a straight face to a friend who has done very little, it's a joke, not praise. Khēba belongs with it: an exclamation of mock disbelief for good-natured teasing among friends. Joking like this is for friends; with elders, a manager or someone you've just met, say things straight.

title: Nice parking, champ! Mock praise
goal: Outside Bū Rāshid's majlis, Rāshid praises your terrible parking; take the joke, and tease him back about his team's defeat
tip: Mock praise uses real compliments for something bad: yā baṭal 'champ', shu hal-mawhiba! 'what talent!', innak fannān 'you're an artist'. The tone and the situation tell everyone it's a joke. When you've both scored a point, call it even: wāḥid wāḥid (you'll hear tʿādalna).
grammar: irony: mock praise (yā baṭal, innak fannān)
dialogue: A
يا سلام! صفيت السيارة عدل، ما شاء الله عليك يا بطل
yā salām! ṣaffēt is-sayyāra ʿadil, mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēk yā baṭal
Wow! You've parked the car so straight; well done, champ! (ironic)
B
أدري، أدري. مايلة، ونصها على الرصيف
adri, adri. māyla, w nuṣṣha ʿala r-raṣīf
I know, I know. It's crooked, and half of it's on the pavement.
A
لا، شو هالموهبة! والله إنك فنان، تستاهل جايزة
la, shu hal-mawhiba! wallāh innak fannān, tistāhil jāyza
No, what talent! Honestly, you're an artist; you deserve a prize. (ironic)
B
مشكور يا كابتن. وفريقك؟ سمعت إنكم خسرتوا أمس
mashkūr yā kābtin. w farīgak? simaʿt innakum khisartu ams
Thanks, captain. And your team? I heard you lost yesterday.
A
خيبة! لا تتطنز علي. منو قال لك؟ أكيد سيف
khēba! la titṭannaz ʿalay. minu gāl-lak? akīd Sēf
Come on! Don't make fun of me. Who told you? It must have been Sēf.
B
محد قال لي. الفيديو في قروب الشباب، يا بطل
maḥḥad gāl-li. il-fīdyo fi grūb ish-shabāb, yā baṭal
Nobody told me. The video's in the lads' group, champ. (ironic)
A
زين زين، تعادلنا. واحد واحد
zēn zēn, tʿādalna. wāḥid wāḥid
OK, OK, we're even. One-all.
B
هيه، واحد واحد. بس بصفها عدل قبل لا يشوفها أبوك
hē, wāḥid wāḥid. bas baṣiffha ʿadil gabil la yshūfha ubūk
Yes, one-all. But I'll park it properly before your dad sees it.
A
تأخرت! شافها من الدريشة وقام يضحك. تعال حبيبي، لا تتهرب!
taʼakhkhart! shāfha min id-dirīsha w gām yiẓḥak. taʿāl ḥabībi, la titharrab!
Too late! He saw it from the window and burst out laughing. Nice try, mate; don't try to dodge it!
B
فشلة! بروح أسلم عليه قبل لا يقول شي
fashla! barūḥ asallim ʿalēh gabil la ygūl shay
How embarrassing! I'll go and say hello to him before he says anything.
items: champ! (ironic, for something done badly) (friends only)
crooked, at an angle, leaning (a feminine thing)
on the pavement, on the kerb
an artist; (ironic) a real artist, a genius

title: The uncle's jokes
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, Sēf is on a video call from abroad, and his uncle jokes he'll come home talking like a foreigner; laugh along and stay respectful
tip: When an elder jokes, join in at your own expense or play along with his joke, and never turn it back on him. ana baʿallmah il-ʿarabi 'I'll teach him Arabic' makes him laugh because it's the wrong way round. When he turns serious, follow him: ṣidagt yā ʿammi.
grammar: irony with elders: playing along respectfully (ana baʿallmah il-ʿarabi, ṣār yilbas…)
dialogue: A
يا حيا الله! تعال يا ولدي، نحن قاعدين نتمصخر على سيف
yā ḥayya allāh! taʿāl yā wildi, niḥin gāʿdīn nitmaṣkhar ʿala Sēf
Welcome! Come in, son; we're having fun at Sēf's expense (on the video call).
B
الله يحييك يا عمي. خير؟ شو سوى؟
allāh yḥayyīk yā ʿammi. khēr? shu sawwa?
Thank you, uncle. What is it? What's he done?
A
سنة في الغربة، وبيرجع يرطن مثل الأجانب، وينسى الكلمات العربية وطعم المجبوس!
sana fi l-ghurba, w biyirjaʿ yirṭin mithil il-ajānib, w yinsa l-kalimāt il-ʿarabiyya w ṭaʿm il-majbūs!
A year abroad, and he'll come back jabbering like a foreigner, forgetting his Arabic words and the taste of majbūs!
B
لا تخاف يا عمي، أنا بعلمه العربي!
la tkhāf yā ʿammi, ana baʿallmah il-ʿarabi!
Don't worry, uncle, I'll teach him Arabic!
A
ما شاء الله! الإنقليزي بيعلم ولد دبي العربي؟ هذي يديدة!
mā shāʼ allāh! il-ingilīzi biyʿallim wild Dbayy il-ʿarabi? hādhi yidīda!
Well I never! The Englishman's going to teach a Dubai lad Arabic? That's a new one!
B
والله يا عمي، صار يلبس بنطلون بدال الكندورة
wallāh yā ʿammi, ṣār yilbas banṭalōn badāl il-kandūra
Honestly, uncle, he's started wearing trousers instead of the kandūra.
A
شفت يا سيف؟ حتى ربيعك صار شاهد عليك!
shift yā Sēf? ḥatta rbīʿak ṣār shāhid ʿalēk!
See, Sēf? Even your friend has become a witness against you!
B
أمزح وياه يا عمي. سيف ما ينسى أهله
amzaḥ wiyyāh yā ʿammi. Sēf ma yinsa ahlah
I'm only teasing him, uncle. Sēf won't forget his family.
A
أدري يا ولدي، هذا كلام مجالس. سيف من صغره دلوع أمه، بس الغربة ما فيها مزح
adri yā wildi, hādha kalām majālis. Sēf min ṣighrah dallūʿ ummah, bas il-ghurba ma fīha mazaḥ
I know, son, that's just majlis talk. Sēf's been his mother's spoilt boy since he was little, but being far from home is no joke.
B
صدقت يا عمي. نشتاق له وايد
ṣidagt yā ʿammi. nishtāg-lah wāyid
That's true, uncle. We miss him a lot.
items: we're joking around, we're making fun (of someone)
(he) jabbers in a foreign language, talks like a foreigner (teasing)
majbūs (spiced rice with meat or fish)
spoilt (a boy or man), a pampered child
culture: Bū Rāshid may tease Sēf, or you, in front of the majlis; you can laugh, play along or joke at your own expense. Keep your jokes away from anything that would embarrass someone: a joke that makes a person lose face reads as disrespect. Friends' words such as yā rayyāl are out of place here: with elders and in official settings they're a real faux pas.

title: Enough now: where banter stops
goal: At a karak stand during Fahad's visit, he teases your classmate Mājid in front of strangers, about a story you once told; stop him kindly, help him put it right
tip: To stop a joke without a fight: khalāṣ ʿād 'that's enough now', then say why: mub jiddām in-nās 'not in front of people', il-ḥīn mub wagtah 'now's not the time'. zawwadt-ha, aḥrajtah 'you went too far, you embarrassed him'; Fahad answers zawwadt-ha 'I went too far' and ḥaggak ʿalay 'I'm sorry'.
grammar: where banter stops: khalāṣ ʿād, zawwadt-ha, mub wagtah
dialogue: A
ماجد يسوق بروحه للجامعة؟ يا بطل! هذا اللي رسب في الليسن ثلاث مرات!
Mājid ysūg b-rūḥah lil-jāmʿa? yā baṭal! hādha illi risab fi l-lēsin thalāth marrāt!
Mājid drives himself to uni now? What a champ! This is the guy who failed his driving test three times!
B
خيبة يا فهد! هذاك من زمان
khēba yā Fahad! hādhāk min zamān
Come off it, Fahad! That was ages ago.
A
وفي المرة الثالثة، المدرب نزل من السيارة وهو يصيح!
w fi l-marra th-thālitha, il-mudarrib nizal min is-sayyāra w huwa yṣīḥ!
(loudly, to the karak man) And the third time, the instructor got out of the car in tears!
B
فهد، خلاص عاد. ماجد ما ضحك
Fahad, khalāṣ ʿād. Mājid ma ẓiḥak
Fahad, that's enough now. Mājid isn't laughing.
A
شفيه؟ أمزح! دمه خفيف، يتحمل
shfīh? amzaḥ! dammah khafīf, yitḥammal
What's up with him? I'm joking! He's a good sport, he can take it.
B
يتحمل ويا الشباب بس، مب قدام الناس. زودتها، أحرجته
yitḥammal wiyya sh-shabāb bas, mub jiddām in-nās. zawwadt-ha, aḥrajtah
He can take it with the lads, not in front of people. You've gone too far; you embarrassed him.
A
والله؟ ما كان قصدي أجرحه
wallāh? ma kān gaṣdi ajraḥah
Really? I didn't mean to hurt him.
B
أدري. بس الحين مب وقته، هالسالفة ما فيها مزح عنده. كلمه
adri. bas il-ḥīn mub wagtah, has-sālfa ma fīha mazaḥ ʿindah. kallmah
I know. But now's not the time; for him, that story's no joke. Talk to him.
A
ماجد، حقك علي يا خوي. زودتها
Mājid, ḥaggak ʿalay yā khūy. zawwadt-ha
Mājid, I'm sorry, bro. I went too far.
B
يلا، الكرك على فهد! وايد عليك
yalla, il-karak ʿala Fahad! wāyid ʿalēk
(to Mājid) Come on, karak's on Fahad! (to Fahad) Steady on, don't overdo it! (ironic)
items: you've gone too far (to a man); I went too far
you embarrassed him (to a man); I embarrassed him
I'm sorry, I owe you an apology (to a man)
to a woman: ḥaggich ʿalay (حقج علي); lit. 'your right is on me'
the driving test; the driving licence (English loan)
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner, talk for 10 minutes about teasing among friends where they grew up: what's fine, and what crosses the line. Tell one short story of a joke that went too far (yours or made up), using khalāṣ ʿād, zawwadt-ha and ḥaggak ʿalay. Then switch register: retell it in 1 minute as if to Bū Rāshid's majlis, respectfully, with no friends' words.

title: The printer hates me: humour at work
goal: At the office, the printer jams again just before a meeting; joke about it with Maryam, keep it polite, and get the copies printed
tip: At work, keep humour light and aim it at things or at yourself: haṭ-ṭābʿa manḥūsa 'this printer's jinxed', killha nakad 'it's nothing but grief'. Maryam's irony is just as gentle: wallāh innak fannān! il-ḥīn iṭ-ṭābʿa ṣārat taʿarf thalāth lughāt 'now the printer knows three languages'.
grammar: light irony at work: joking about yourself (ḥaẓẓi, kill ma)
dialogue: A
الطابعة علقت مرة ثانية؟ شكلها تكرهك
iṭ-ṭābʿa ʿilgat marra thānya? shaklha tikrahak
The printer's jammed again? Looks like it hates you.
B
هيه، هالطابعة منحوسة، كلها نكد
hē, haṭ-ṭābʿa manḥūsa, killha nakad
Yes, this printer's jinxed; it's nothing but grief.
A
كل ما تقرب منها تخرب، وقدام الناس بعد! والله ما شفت جي
kill ma tgarrib minha tikhrab, w jiddām in-nās baʿad! wallāh ma shift chī
Every time you go near it, it breaks down, and in front of everyone too! Honestly, I've never seen anything like it.
B
حظي. يمكن طفشانة وتبي إجازة مثلي
ḥaẓẓi. yimkin ṭafshāna w tabi ijāza mithli
That's my luck. Maybe it's fed up and wants a holiday, like me.
A
إجازة؟ مب وقته! انت توك راجع من إجازة
ijāza? mub wagtah! inta tawwak rājiʿ min ijāza
A holiday? Not now! You've only just come back from one.
B
صح، بس مزاجها اليوم مب زين. تقدرين تطبعين من فوق؟
ṣaḥḥ, bas mizājha l-yōm mub zēn. tigdarīn tiṭbaʿīn min fōg?
True, but it's in a bad mood today. Could you print upstairs?
A
زين، بطبع النسخ من طابعة الدور الثاني. وانت شوف الحبر والورقة، لا تتهرب!
zēn, baṭbaʿ in-nusakh min ṭābʿat id-dōr ith-thāni. w inta shūf il-ḥibir w il-warga, la titharrab!
OK, I'll print the copies on the printer on the second floor. And you check the ink and the paper; don't try to dodge it!
B
لقيت الورقة! يمكن كانت تبي أحد يكلمها بالعربي
ligēt il-warga! yimkin kānat tabi aḥad ykallimha bil-ʿarabi
Found the paper! Maybe it wanted someone to talk to it in Arabic.
A
والله إنك فنان! الحين الطابعة صارت تعرف ثلاث لغات
wallāh innak fannān! il-ḥīn iṭ-ṭābʿa ṣārat taʿarf thalāth lughāt
Honestly, you're a genius! Now the printer knows three languages.
B
على الأقل أحد يتعلم مني! يلا، الاجتماع بعد خمس دقايق
ʿala l-aqall aḥad yitʿallam minni! yalla, il-ijtimāʿ baʿd khams dagāyig
At least someone's learning from me! Come on, the meeting's in five minutes.
items: grief, misery, a downer (something that spoils your mood)
a woman, or a feminine thing: ṭafshāna (طفشانة)
her mood, its mood (a feminine thing)
culture: Maryam and B aim the jokes at the printer and keep any teasing gentle: humour between colleagues stays light, and it stays polite. Khēba and yā rayyāl are words for friends; a woman colleague, a manager or a client hears plain, friendly Arabic.

title: I won't do it again
goal: On the phone, Rāshid is cool with you after your joke about his school marks in front of his dad's guests; apologise properly and make it up to him
tip: A real apology after a joke has no excuses: aʿtadhir minnak, ḥaggak ʿalay, ma baʿīd-ha 'I won't do it again'. Say what was wrong (kānat sakhīfa 'it was a stupid joke', mub jiddām in-nās), and let him have his say: gahartni wallāh 'you really got to me'.
grammar: after a joke goes wrong: apologising without excuses (aʿtadhir minnak, ma baʿīd-ha)
dialogue: B
هلا راشد، شحالك؟
hala Rāshid, shḥālak?
Hi Rāshid, how are you?
A
بخير، الله يسلمك. خير؟
b-khēr, allāh ysallmak. khēr?
Fine, thanks. What's up?
B
أبي أعتذر منك. النكتة اللي قلتها عن درجاتك في المجلس كانت سخيفة
abi aʿtadhir minnak. in-nukta illi gilt-ha ʿan darajātak fi l-majlis kānat sakhīfa
I want to apologise to you. That joke I made about your marks in the majlis was stupid.
A
هيه برو، قدام أبوي والضيوف. حسيت إني ياهل، خربت برستيجي!
hē brō, jiddām ubūy w iẓ-ẓyūf. ḥassēt inni yāhil, kharrabt barstīji!
Yeah, bro, in front of my dad and the guests. I felt like a little kid; you wrecked my image!
B
معك حق. زودتها، حقك علي، ما بعيدها
maʿak ḥagg. zawwadt-ha, ḥaggak ʿalay, ma baʿīd-ha
You're right. I went too far; I'm sorry. I won't do it again.
A
أدري إنك تمزح، بس أنا رسبت في الرياضيات، وأبوي للحين عتبان
adri innak timzaḥ, bas ana rasabt fi r-riyāẓiyyāt, w ubūy lil-ḥīn ʿatbān
I know you were joking, but I failed maths, and my dad's still upset about it.
B
فهمت. كان المفروض أمزح وياك بروحنا، مب قدام الناس
fhimt. kān il-mafrūẓ amzaḥ wiyyāk b-rūḥna, mub jiddām in-nās
I get it. I should have joked with you when it was just us, not in front of people.
A
خلاص، انسى السالفة. بس قهرتني والله، والبرجر عليك
khalāṣ, insa s-sālfa. bas gahartni wallāh, w il-bargar ʿalēk
OK, forget it. But you really got to me, so the burger's on you.
B
اتفقنا! وولا كلمة عن الدرجات بعد اليوم
ittafagna! w wala kilma ʿan id-darajāt baʿd il-yōm
Deal! And not a word about marks from today on.
A
زين، انت تمون. بس إذا قلت إنك تعرف تلعب كورة، بقول لك: أونه!
zēn, inta tmūn. bas idha gilt innak taʿarf tilʿab kūra, bagūl-lak: awinna!
Fine, you're one of us. But if you say you can play football, I'll say: yeah, right!
items: stupid, silly, lame (a joke, an idea; a feminine thing)
your image, your standing, face (English loan)
I failed (an exam); you failed (to a man)
to a woman: rasabti (رسبتي); he failed: risab (رسب)
upset (with someone), hurt and cross (a man)
you really upset me, you got to me (to a man)
you're close enough (to ask or joke), you're one of us (to a man)

title: Can you do it cheaper?
goal: At the office, a client says your offer is too expensive; hold the price politely, and (as Bū Saʿīd allows) give a small discount for a quick deal
tip: Don't drop the price at once. Show what he gets (nkhalliṣ gabil il-mawʿid b-usbūʿ), ask for something back (ʿala sharṭ twaggʿūn il-ʿagid hal-usbūʿ) and keep the respect (ṭāl ʿumrak). ṣaddigni 'believe me' backs a point, but use it once, not in every line.
grammar: negotiating: giving something in return (ʿala sharṭ…, nafs is-siʿir bas…)
dialogue: A
العرض زين، بس السعر غالي شوي. ما تقدرون تنزلون السعر؟
il-ʿarẓ zēn, bas is-siʿir ghāli shwayy. ma tigdarūn tnazzlūn is-siʿir?
The offer's good, but the price is a bit high. Can't you bring it down?
B
أفهمك، طال عمرك. بس صدقني، شغلنا يستاهل
afhamak, ṭāl ʿumrak. bas ṣaddigni, shughulna yistāhil
I understand, sir. But believe me, our work is worth it.
A
كل ما أكلم شركة تقول جي. وفي شركة ثانية عرضها مغري، أرخص منكم
kill ma akallim sharika tgūl chī. w fī sharika thānya ʿarẓha mughri, arkhaṣ minkum
Every company I talk to says that. And there's another company whose offer's tempting; it's cheaper than you.
B
يمكن، بس من صوب ثاني، بيخلصون على الوقت؟
yimkin, bas min ṣōb thāni, biykhallṣūn ʿala l-wagt?
Maybe, but on the other hand, will they finish on time?
A
هذا اللي ما أدريه. بشكل عام الميزانية عندنا محدودة، شو بتعطوني زيادة؟
hādha illi ma adrīh. bi-shakl ʿāmm il-mīzāniyya ʿindana maḥdūda, shu bitaʿṭūni ziyāda?
That I don't know. On the whole our budget's limited; what will you give me on top?
B
في جملة وحدة: نفس السعر، بس نخلص قبل الموعد بأسبوع، والتدريب علينا
fi jumla waḥda: nafs is-siʿir, bas nkhalliṣ gabil il-mawʿid b-usbūʿ, w it-tadrīb ʿalēna
In a nutshell: the same price, but we finish a week before the deadline, and the training's on us.
A
عرض مب شين. بس المدير عندي مزاجه صعب، والسعر ثابت؟
ʿarẓ mub shēn. bas il-mudīr ʿindi mizājah ṣaʿb, w is-siʿir thābit?
Not a bad offer. But my manager's hard to please; and is the price fixed?
B
مب ثابت، بو سعيد مرن. نقدر، على شرط توقعون العقد هالأسبوع
mub thābit, Bū Saʿīd marin. nigdar, ʿala sharṭ twaggʿūn il-ʿagid hal-usbūʿ
It isn't fixed; Bū Saʿīd is flexible. We can, on condition you sign the contract this week.
A
اتفقنا. بس لازم أشاور المدير أول
ittafagna. bas lāzim ashāwir il-mudīr awwal
Agreed. But I have to check with my manager first.
B
على راحتك. بنطرش لك العرض الأخير اليوم
ʿala rāḥtak. binṭarrish-lak il-ʿarẓ il-akhīr il-yōm
Take your time. We'll send you the final offer today.
items: limited (a budget, time; a feminine thing)

title: Just try it for a month
goal: At the office, persuade your manager, Bū Saʿīd, to try your idea of one shared task list for a month, and answer his doubts
tip: Make a new idea feel safe: keep it small (shahar wāḥid bas, tajruba), say what happens if it fails (lō ma nifaʿ, nirjaʿ lil-īmēl), and offer to do the work yourself (ana basawwīha). Then wait for agnaʿtni 'you've convinced me'.
grammar: persuading: lowering the risk (lō ma nifaʿ…, hal-marra ghēr)
dialogue: B
طال عمرك، عندي فكرة للفريق. تسمح لي دقيقتين؟
ṭāl ʿumrak, ʿindi fikra lil-farīg. tismaḥ-li digīgtēn?
Sir, I've got an idea for the team. Can you spare me two minutes?
A
تفضل، بس بسرعة، عندي اجتماع
tfaẓẓal, bas b-surʿa, ʿindi ijtimāʿ
Go ahead, but quickly; I've got a meeting.
B
الإيميلات صارت فوضى، والشغل مشتت. نبي قايمة وحدة على النت
il-īmēlāt ṣārat fawẓa, w ish-shughul mshattat. nabi gāyma waḥda ʿala n-nit
The emails have become a mess, and the work's all over the place. We need one list online.
A
جربنا جي قبل، وصار كل شي متلخبط. الكل رجع للإيميل
jarrabna chī gabil, w ṣār kill shay mitlakhbiṭ. il-kill rijaʿ lil-īmēl
We tried that before, and everything got muddled. Everyone went back to email.
B
هالمرة غير. القايمة تنظم الشغل، وأنا بسويها
hal-marra ghēr. il-gāyma tnaẓẓim ish-shughul, w ana basawwīha
This time's different. The list organises the work, and I'll set it up.
A
وإذا صار الشغل ممل؟ لازم أشاور الفريق أول
w idha ṣār ish-shughul mumill? lāzim ashāwir il-farīg awwal
And if the work gets tedious? I have to check with the team first.
B
شهر واحد بس، تجربة. لو ما نفع، نرجع للإيميل
shahar wāḥid bas, tajruba. lō ma nifaʿ, nirjaʿ lil-īmēl
Just one month, as a trial. If it doesn't work, we go back to email.
A
كلامك منطقي، والفكرة مب شين. بس منو بيتابع الشغل كل أسبوع؟
kalāmak manṭiqi, w il-fikra mub shēn. bas minu biytābiʿ ish-shughul kill usbūʿ?
That makes sense, and the idea's not bad. But who's going to keep track of the work every week?
B
أنا. وكل خميس بطرش لك ملخص
ana. w kill khamīs baṭarrish-lak mulakhkhaṣ
Me. And every Thursday I'll send you a summary.
A
زين، أقنعتني، وأنا مرن. شهر واحد، على شرط تتابعها بنفسك
zēn, agnaʿtni, w ana marin. shahar wāḥid, ʿala sharṭ titābiʿha b-nafsak
All right, you've convinced me, and I'm flexible. One month, on condition you keep track of it yourself.
items: (it, f.) organises; you organise (to a man)
to a woman: tnaẓẓmīn (تنظمين); he organises: ynaẓẓim (ينظم)

title: I'll vouch for him
goal: On the phone, tell your landlord your flatmate is moving out, and persuade him to accept the colleague who'll move in instead
tip: Persuade from your record: inta taʿarfni min yōm ma sikant 'you've known me since I moved in'. If it's good, he'll add to it: ʿumrak ma taʼakhkhart. Vouch for the other man (wild ḥalāl, mʼaddab w rizīn), and take the risk on yourself: ana aẓmanah, w ʿala masʼūliyyti.
grammar: persuading from your record (min yōm ma…, ʿumrak ma…, ʿala masʼūliyyti)
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم، طال عمرك. تسمح لي دقيقتين؟
as-salāmu ʿalaykum, ṭāl ʿumrak. tismaḥ-li digīgtēn?
Hello, sir. Can you spare me two minutes?
A
وعليكم السلام، هلا يا سالم. آمر؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām, hala yā Sālim. āmir?
Hello, Sālim. What can I do for you?
B
ربيعي اللي ساكن معاي بيطلع آخر الشهر
rbīʿi illi sākin maʿāy biyiṭlaʿ ākhir ish-shahar
My friend who lives with me is moving out at the end of the month.
A
زين تسوي إنك قلت لي. بس ترا أنا أفضل أعطيها عايلة، مب عزوبي
zēn tsawwi innak gilt-li. bas tara ana afaẓẓil aʿṭīha ʿāyla, mub ʿazūbi
Good of you to tell me. But I'd rather let it to a family, you know, not a bachelor.
B
أنا باقي. وبيسكن معاي زميل من الدوام
ana bāgi. w biyiskin maʿāy zamīl min id-dawām
I'm staying. And a colleague from work is going to live with me.
A
بس أنا ما أعرفه. وإذا سوى ضجة، منو بيضمن لي؟
bas ana ma aʿarfah. w idha sawwa ẓajja, minu biyiẓman-li?
But I don't know him. And if he makes a racket, who's going to guarantee me?
B
ولد حلال، مؤدب ورزين. أنا أضمنه، وعلى مسؤوليتي
wild ḥalāl, mʼaddab w rizīn. ana aẓmanah, w ʿala masʼūliyyti
He's a decent guy, well-mannered and level-headed. I vouch for him, on my responsibility.
A
صح، وعمرك ما تأخرت علي في الإيجار
ṣaḥḥ, w ʿumrak ma taʼakhkhart ʿalay fi l-ījār
True, and you've never once been late with the rent.
B
وانت تعرفني من يوم ما سكنت. إذا تقدر، تعال السبت وتتعرف عليه
w inta taʿarfni min yōm ma sikant. idha tigdar, taʿāl is-sabt w titʿarraf ʿalēh
And you've known me since the day I moved in. If you can, come on Saturday and meet him.
A
زين، أقنعتني، وأنا مرن. السبت بعد العصر، وإذا عجبني نتفاهم
zēn, agnaʿtni, w ana marin. is-sabt baʿd il-ʿaṣir, w idha ʿajabni nitfāham
All right, you've convinced me, and I'm flexible. Saturday after ʿaṣr, and if I like him, we'll come to an arrangement.
items: what can I do for you? (lit. command me) (respectful)
a decent guy, a good man (lit. a lawful son)
task: This week: in Talk, ask your partner to play your landlord, who doesn't want a stranger in his flat. Persuade him for 10 turns, respectfully (ṭāl ʿumrak, ʿala masʼūliyyti, min yōm ma…). Then switch register: record a 2-minute voice note telling Sēf how it went, as friends talk, with a joke or two. Keep to what each person says: no rules, prices or official steps.

title: One condition
goal: At your flat on Saturday, your colleague is held up at work, but the landlord likes what he sees; agree to his condition, and get your own small request in
tip: When the other side sets a condition, accept it clearly (ma ykhālif, w ʿala masʼūliyyti), then make your own request straight away, while he's pleased: bas ʿindi ṭalab ṣghīr. Keep it small and concrete, and he can agree without losing face.
grammar: negotiating: accepting a condition and asking in return (ma ykhālif…, bas ʿindi ṭalab ṣaghīr)
dialogue: A
ما شاء الله، الشقة نظيفة! أحسن من يوم سلمتها لك
mā shāʼ allāh, ish-shigga naẓīfa! aḥsan min yōm sallamt-ha lak
Mā shāʼ allāh, the flat's spotless! Better than the day I handed it over to you.
B
تسلم طال عمرك. زميلي من الدوام تأخر، بيمر عليك بعدين
tislam ṭāl ʿumrak. zamīli min id-dawām taʼakhkhar, biymurr ʿalēk baʿdēn
Thank you, sir. My colleague from work is held up; he'll come by later.
A
الله يسلمك. ما يخالف، باين إنه ولد حلال. والأثاث؟ كله زين؟
allāh ysallmak. ma ykhālif, bāyin innah wild ḥalāl. w il-athāth? killah zēn?
You're welcome. No problem; he sounds like a decent guy. And the furniture? Is it all OK?
B
كله زين، بس الحنفية في المطبخ خربانة، والصبغ في الغرفة الثانية قديم
killah zēn, bas il-ḥanafiyya fi l-maṭbakh kharbāna, w iṣ-ṣabigh fi l-ghurfa th-thānya gadīm
It's all fine, but the kitchen tap's broken, and the paint in the second room is old.
A
زين. بس عندي شرط: ما في ضجة، والعقد يبقى باسمك، وانت المسؤول
zēn. bas ʿindi sharṭ: ma fī ẓajja, w il-ʿagid yibga b-ismak, w inta l-masʼūl
Fine. But I have a condition: no noise, the contract stays in your name, and you're the one responsible.
B
ما يخالف، وعلى مسؤوليتي. بس عندي طلب صغير
ma ykhālif, w ʿala masʼūliyyti. bas ʿindi ṭalab ṣghīr
No problem; it's on me. But I've got a small request.
A
خير؟ قول
khēr? gūl
What is it? Go on.
B
الصيانة تصلح الحنفية، وتصبغ الغرفة قبل لا يسكن
iṣ-ṣiyāna tṣalliḥ il-ḥanafiyya, w tiṣbugh il-ghurfa gabil la yiskin
Could maintenance fix the tap, and paint the room before he moves in?
A
هذا حقك. بطرش لك الصيانة يوم الأحد، والبلاط بعد بنشوفه
hādha ḥaggak. baṭarrish-lak iṣ-ṣiyāna yōm il-aḥad, w il-balāṭ baʿad binshūfah
That's your right. I'll send maintenance round on Sunday, and we'll look at the tiles too.
B
اتفقنا. وإن شاء الله يسكن السبت الياي
ittafagna. w in shāʼ allāh yiskin is-sabt il-yāy
Deal. And, God willing, he moves in next Saturday.
items: the paint (on a wall, a car)

title: Time for a new car?
goal: At a karak stand, your classmate Khalfān says it's time to change your old car and pushes a big one; argue for a small one, and agree to see one he knows
tip: Persuasion between friends goes both ways. Khalfān pushes (ismaʿni…, yā shēkh, il-ḥajim muhimm); you answer with your own priorities: ish-shakil mub kill shay 'looks aren't everything', ma abi aṣrif wāyid. Before you say yes, check: la ykūn fīha shay? 'there's nothing wrong with it, is there?'
grammar: persuading a friend: pushing and pushing back (ismaʿni…, mub kill shay)
dialogue: A
سيارتك خربت مرة ثانية؟ خلاص يا ريّال، لازم تبدلها
sayyārtak khirbat marra thānya? khalāṣ yā rayyāl, lāzim tbaddilha
Your car's broken down again? That's it, man; you have to change it.
B
أدري، بس ما أبي أصرف وايد
adri, bas ma abi aṣrif wāyid
I know, but I don't want to spend a lot.
A
اسمعني، خذ لك سيارة كبيرة. تروح البر، تروح حتا، ولا شي يوقفك
ismaʿni, khudh-lak sayyāra kbīra. trūḥ il-barr, trūḥ Ḥatta, wala shay ywaggfak
Listen to me, get yourself a big car. You can go to the desert, to Hatta, and nothing will stop you.
B
والبترول؟ أنا أبي وحدة صغيرة
w il-batrōl? ana abi waḥda ṣghīra
And the petrol? I want a small one.
A
صغيرة؟ يا شيخ! الحجم مهم، والكبيرة تاكل بترول شوي بس
ṣghīra? yā shēkh! il-ḥajim muhimm, w il-kbīra tākil batrōl shwayy bas
Small? Come on! Size matters, and a big one only uses a little petrol.
B
الشكل مب كل شي. أهم شي ما تخرب كل أسبوع
ish-shakil mub kill shay. ahamm shay ma tikhrab kill usbūʿ
Looks aren't everything. The main thing is it doesn't break down every week.
A
زين، أقنعتني. في واحد أعرفه يبيع سيارته، صغيرة ونظيفة، وسعرها مب شين
zēn, agnaʿtni. fī wāḥid aʿarfah ybīʿ sayyārtah, ṣghīra w naẓīfa, w siʿrha mub shēn
OK, you've convinced me. There's a guy I know selling his car; it's small and in good condition, and the price isn't bad.
B
صج؟ ليش يبيعها؟ لا يكون فيها شي
ṣij? lēsh ybīʿha? la ykūn fīha shay
Really? Why's he selling it? There isn't something wrong with it, is there?
A
لا، بيسافر ويبي يبيعها بسرعة
la, biysāfir w yabi ybīʿha b-surʿa
No, he's going abroad and wants to sell it quickly.
B
ما يخالف، بس بشوفها أول، وبسوي لها فحص
ma ykhālif, bas bashūfha awwal, w basawwī-lha faḥiṣ
Fine, but I'll see it first and get it inspected.
items: I don't want to spend a lot
UAE also: ma abā aṣrif (ما أبا أصرف)
(it, f.) burns petrol, uses petrol (lit. eats petrol)
(recognise); a thirsty car: tākil batrōl wāyid
clean; in good condition (a car, a flat)
I'm selling my car: abīʿ sayyārti (أبيع سيارتي)
an inspection, a check-up (of a car)
I'll get it (f.) inspected: basawwī-lha faḥiṣ (بسوي لها فحص)

title: Cash today? That's different
goal: At the seller's house, look over the small car Khalfān found for you, resist his pressure, and agree a discount for cash after this afternoon's inspection
tip: Answer pressure calmly: if he says someone else wants it, let him (khallah yākhidh-ha). Show you're serious (ana jādd), then offer what he wants most in return for what you want: idha l-faḥiṣ ṭilaʿ zēn, adfaʿ-lak kāsh il-yōm, bas tnazzil shwayy.
grammar: negotiating: calling a bluff, then trading (khallah yākhidh-ha, idha…, bas…)
dialogue: A
هذي هي. شوف العداد، ما مشت وايد، ونظيفة من داخل ومن برا
hādhi hiya. shūf il-ʿaddād, ma mishat wāyid, w naẓīfa min dākhil w min barra
Here it is. Look at the meter: it hasn't done many kilometres, and it's clean inside and out.
B
ما شاء الله، حلوة. بس فيها خدش هني
mā shāʼ allāh, ḥilwa. bas fīha khadish hni
Mā shāʼ allāh, it's nice. But there's a scratch here.
A
الخدش بسيط، والسيارة ما عليها ولا دعمة. والمكينة زينة
il-khadish basīṭ, w is-sayyāra ma ʿalēha wala dʿma. w il-makīna zēna
The scratch is nothing, and the car hasn't had a single knock. And the engine's good.
B
بس سعرها غالي شوي. ما أبي أصرف وايد
bas siʿrha ghāli shwayy. ma abi aṣrif wāyid
But it's a bit expensive. I don't want to spend a lot.
A
السعر ثابت. وترا في واحد ثاني يبيها اليوم
is-siʿir thābit. w tara fī wāḥid thāni yabīha l-yōm
The price is fixed. And there's someone else who wants it today, you know.
B
خله ياخذها. أنا جاد، بس ما بدفع أكثر
khallah yākhidhha. ana jādd, bas ma badfaʿ akthar
Let him have it. I'm serious, but I won't pay more.
A
زين، شو تبي؟
zēn, shu tabi?
All right, what do you want?
B
إذا الفحص طلع زين، أدفع لك كاش اليوم. بس تنزل شوي
idha l-faḥiṣ ṭilaʿ zēn, adfaʿ-lak kāsh il-yōm. bas tnazzil shwayy
If the inspection comes back fine, I'll pay you cash today. But you knock a bit off.
A
كاش اليوم؟ هذا كلام ثاني. ما يخالف، بس عطني عربون الحين
kāsh il-yōm? hādha kalām thāni. ma ykhālif, bas ʿaṭni ʿarbūn il-ḥīn
Cash today? That's a different matter. Fine by me, but give me a deposit now.
B
تفضل العربون. والفحص العصر إن شاء الله
tfaẓẓal il-ʿarbūn. w il-faḥiṣ il-ʿaṣir in shāʼ allāh
Here's the deposit. And the inspection's this afternoon, God willing.
items: it (f.) hasn't done many kilometres (a car; lit. it hasn't walked much)
a knock, a bump (a minor accident)
culture: When someone shows you something new, Gulf speakers admire it with mā shāʼ allāh, to praise it without envy. So B starts with mā shāʼ allāh even while he points out the scratch.
